record.text: Among Horizon 2020 volcanology projects with an Italian participating organisation, what approaches to monitoring volcanic unrest and forecasting eruptions are being developed?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id JOIN organization o ON o.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/volcanology%' AND o.country = 'IT' ORDER BY p.id

record.reference_answer: Eight of the fifteen Italian-participating volcanology projects develop such approaches, in three families. New instrumentation: NEWTON-g builds a field gravity imager - an array of low-cost MEMS relative gravimeters anchored on an absolute quantum gravimeter - deployed at Etna to image subsurface mass change continuously, while SiC nano for PicoGeo develops 3C-SiC optical nano-strain-meters (target resolution 10-12) to reveal the slow strain transients that precede eruptions, seeding a 'Pico strain Etna Lab'. Automated interpretation of monitoring signals: VULCAN.ears builds a volcano-independent automatic Volcano-Seismic Recognition system, based on structured Hidden Markov Models and a Parallel System Architecture, so observatories can classify precursory seismicity in real time, and ARISE2 turns its infrasound and lidar network into a Volcano Information System, calibrated using Etna monitoring, that estimates ash plume height and mass eruption rate remotely for aviation security. Modelling, imaging and shared infrastructure: PICVOLC jointly inverts seismic, gravity and deformation data with 3D Finite Element modelling to image the source of volcanic unrest at Nevado del Ruiz; IMPROVE images magma storage zones by combining seismic, geodetic, gravity and geochemical data with machine learning, and tests fibre-optic sensing and gas and steam monitoring prototypes at Etna and Krafla; ChEESE prepares exascale flagship codes for ensemble volcanic ash dispersal forecasting with satellite data assimilation and physics-based probabilistic volcanic hazard assessment; and EUROVOLC connects volcano observatories and research institutions, integrating modelling of pre-eruption data and virtual access to tools for responding to volcanic unrest and eruptions.
record.notes: FILTER: projects carrying a euroSciVoc path under volcanology (natural sciences/earth and related environmental sciences/geology/volcanology) that have at least one participating organisation in Italy (organization.country='IT', any role). Executed this pass: 15 survivors, against 62 projects carrying the volcanology tag overall, so 47 topic members fail the country filter. ADJUDICATION (exhaustive, S=15 <= 20; every survivor's objective+teaser read, plus report summary/finalResults for the four borderline cases 653980, 674907, 858092, 101025887). IN: 653980 ARISE2 - final results report a Volcano Information System implemented on the ARISE infrasound platform, calibrated using Etna monitoring, for remote monitoring of non-instrumented volcanoes and prediction of ash plume height and mass eruption rate; 731070 EUROVOLC - networks volcano observatories, integrated modelling of pre-eruption data and virtual access to tools for responding to volcanic unrest and eruptions; 749249 VULCAN.ears - automatic Volcano-Seismic Recognition system (structured HMMs + Parallel System Architecture) for real-time monitoring and eruption forecasting; 793811 PICVOLC - joint 3D numerical inversion of seismic, gravity and deformation data with FEM to image the source of volcanic unrest; 801221 NEWTON-g - MEMS/quantum gravimeter array as a field gravity imager for real-time monitoring of subsurface mass change at Etna; 823844 ChEESE - exascale codes for volcano monitoring, ensemble ash dispersal forecast with data assimilation, early-warning and physics-based hazard assessment; 858092 IMPROVE - subsurface imaging of magma systems plus fibre-optic sensing and gas/steam monitoring device prototypes at Etna and Krafla, explicitly to enhance eruption forecasting; 863220 SiC nano for PicoGeo - 3C-SiC optical nano-strain-meters for detecting pre-eruptive strain transients, with a monitoring-network start-up at Etna. OUT: 658591 CIAO - petrology/geochemistry of Iranian ophiolite peridotites, no observation or forecasting method for active volcanoes; 674907 EVER-EST - generic Virtual Research Environment for Earth Science data and workflow preservation; its volcano/supersite use case consumes and shares data, it develops no monitoring or forecasting approach; 714936 TRUE DEPTHS - X-ray-diffraction elastic thermobarometry on UHP rocks to constrain subduction depths; 765710 INSIGHTS - statistics for particle physics, volcanology only as a secondment domain; 845115 ICELEARNING - AI classification of insoluble particles in ice cores (volcanic tephra as a particle class), a palaeoclimate analysis routine; 101024337 PUSKURUM - tephrostratigraphy of past Central Anatolian eruptions for retrospective hazard assessment, no monitoring or forecasting method developed (third parties installing instruments on Erciyes is a reported societal effect, not project work); 101025887 ENDGAME - shock-tube/jet-flow experiments and 3D magma-ascent modelling of basaltic fragmentation, process understanding rather than monitoring or forecasting capability. FILTER LOAD-BEARING: unscoped pooled search for the same question returns volcanology-tagged projects with no Italian participant that satisfy the textual requirement - 798480 VOLCANOWAVES (ES; automatic volcano-seismic detection for eruption forecast modelling), 866085 DEEPVOLC (UK; deep learning on Sentinel-1 deformation to forecast volcanic activity), 789887 TREMOR (IS; pre-eruptive tremor as an eruption precursor), 101003173 MAST (UK/CZ/FR; strain tomography of volcano deformation to interpret unrest signals), 787399 SEISMAZE (FR; tremor analysis for new monitoring and forecasting approaches). Verified by SQL that each carries the volcanology tag and has no IT organisation. TEXT LOAD-BEARING: no stored column records what monitoring or forecasting approach a project develops; the answer exists only in objective and report free text. RETRIEVABILITY: scoped pooled search (k=10 over the 15 survivors) ranks all eight gold members in at least one condition's top-10 (PICVOLC 1/1/1/1, VULCAN.ears 7/2/2/2, SiC nano 2/6/4/3, ARISE2 8/3/6/4, EUROVOLC 3/4/3/6, IMPROVE 5/5/5/5, NEWTON-g 10/7/9/9, ChEESE 9/-/10/8 as lexical/dense/hybrid/hybrid_rerank). TERM_STYLE exact-term: the question reuses vocabulary present verbatim in gold texts - 'volcanic unrest' (PICVOLC, EUROVOLC), 'eruption forecasting' / 'forecasting volcanic eruptions' (VULCAN.ears, SiC nano), 'volcano monitoring' (ARISE2, ChEESE, IMPROVE); consistent with strong lexical ranks for four gold members. Adjudication came from the exhaustive read; the scoped pooled search supplied pooled_candidate_count (11 of the 15 survivors surfaced) and the rank matrix only.

evidence:
Filter (executed this pass, true survivor count 15, <= 200):
SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p
JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id
JOIN organization o ON o.projectID = p.id
WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/volcanology%' AND o.country = 'IT'
ORDER BY p.id
-> 15 survivors: 653980 ARISE2, 658591 CIAO, 674907 EVER-EST, 714936 TRUE DEPTHS, 731070 EUROVOLC, 749249 VULCAN.ears, 765710 INSIGHTS, 793811 PICVOLC, 801221 NEWTON-g, 823844 ChEESE, 845115 ICELEARNING, 858092 IMPROVE, 863220 SiC nano for PicoGeo, 101024337 PUSKURUM, 101025887 ENDGAME.
Topic total without the country condition: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT projectID) FROM euroscivoc WHERE euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/volcanology%' -> 62, i.e. 47 topic members are removed by the Italian-participant condition.

Gold members, with the passages that satisfy the question (verbatim):

653980 ARISE2 - report finalResults: "The Volcano Information System (VIS) implemented in the ARISE platform and presently calibrated using Etna monitoring will be very relevant for remote monitoring of non-instrumented volcanoes. The ARISE team demonstrated the possibility to predict the ash plume height and mass eruption rate based on the infrasound signals associated to the eruptions with a large impact for the aviation security." Objective: "ARISE2 proposes infrasound remote volcano monitoring to provide notifications to civil aviation."

731070 EUROVOLC - objective: "Joint research activities include production of services to initialize volcanic ash transport and dispersal models during eruptions, integrated modelling of pre-eruption data, and a complete catalogue of European Volcanoes. Trans-national access to European Volcano observatories will be facilitated and virtual access to various modelling and assessment tools for responding to volcanic unrest and eruptions will be offered."

749249 VULCAN.ears - objective: "The aim of this proposal is to build an automatic VSR system focused on recognising events in unsupervised scenarios, robust enough to be integrated into the VM centre of any volcano, allowing online risk assessment by real-time seismicity analysis. It will be based on state-of-the-art VSR technologies: a) class description by statistical means (structured Hidden Markov Models) and b) Parallel System Architecture (PSA-VSR) composed of specialised recognition channels"; report summary: "the main input used for eruption forecasting and early warning systems."

793811 PICVOLC - objective: "PICVOLC aims to overcome the limitations in the current approach in the modeling of volcanic unrest by developing a new, original methodology that integrates seismic, gravity, and deformation data with 3D numerical inversion to create a detailed representation of the source of volcanic unrest... PICVOLC involves the integration of fieldwork with Finite Element Methods modeling and joint numerical inversions of geodetic and geophysical data."

801221 NEWTON-g - objective: "We aim at developing a field-compatible gravity imager able to real-time monitor the evolution of the subsurface mass changes through continuous images of the gravity field. This system will include an array of low-costs MEMS-based relative gravimeters anchored on an absolute quantum gravimeter... We will deploy the new gravity imager at Etna volcano (Italy)"; finalResults: "NEWTON-g will thus help to take a step forward in volcano monitoring, through opening a new window for hazard assessment."

823844 ChEESE - objective: "data analysis and predictive techniques for earthquake and volcano monitoring... ensemble-based volcanic ash dispersal, faster than real-time tsunami simulations and physics-based hazard assessments for seismics, volcanoes and tsunamis"; finalResults: "High-resolution volcanic ash dispersal simulations for hazard assessment and operational forecast using data assimilation (ECC8)... Volcanic ash dispersal forecasts at unprecedented resolution (few km) based on satellite data assimilation and ensemble forecast."

858092 IMPROVE - report summary: "It produced new methods to image magma storage zones and to link seismic, geodetic, and geochemical observations across scales. It also created prototypes for advanced gas and steam monitoring devices, demonstrated new uses of fibre-optic sensing for volcano monitoring"; finalResults: "IMPROVE pioneered new techniques for subsurface imaging, combining seismic, geodetic, gravity, and geochemical data with machine learning and numerical modelling... Improved understanding of subsurface processes directly enhances eruption forecasting and volcanic hazard assessment."

863220 SiC nano for PicoGeo - objective: "The goal is the development of a radically new dynamic ground strain measurement technology with an ultra-high resolution of 10-12... Ultra small and slow strain transients preceding earthquakes and eruptions could be revealed... the project outcomes will have direct implications in forecasting volcanic eruptions and thus improve volcano-seismic crisis management. At the end of the project a start-up of one innovative frontier laboratory for advanced monitoring of dynamic strain associated to volcanic and seismic processes will be done. This 'Pico strain Etna Lab' will be the starting point of a new network infrastructure".

Survivors adjudicated OUT (7), with the text that decides them:
- 658591 CIAO: "CIAO will study the amphibole-bearing peridotites of Nain ophiolite (Iran)... measuring major, trace and volatile element concentrations" - laboratory petrology; volcano hazards only as a distant hope ("hoping to reduce the hazards"). No monitoring or forecasting approach.
- 674907 EVER-EST: "developing a generic Virtual Research Environment (VRE) providing earth scientists with the means to manage both the data involved in their disciplines and the scientific methods applied in their observations" - data/workflow infrastructure; the volcano-related use cases are user communities ("disaster and risk management teams (Supersites use case)"), not an approach the project develops.
- 714936 TRUE DEPTHS: "will develop X-ray diffraction analysis of the anisotropic elastic interactions of inclusion minerals trapped inside host minerals" to determine subduction depths - no volcano observation or forecasting.
- 765710 INSIGHTS: "develop advanced statistical methods... to solve problems in Particle Physics"; volcanology appears only as a secondment field ("secondments with partners in other disciplines such as Finance, Climate Science and Volcanology").
- 845115 ICELEARNING: "a two-phase routine for the automatic quantification of insoluble particles trapped in ice cores" - tephra is one particle class in a palaeoclimate routine; no volcano monitoring.
- 101024337 PUSKURUM: "their chemical composition and eruption ages will be determined in the laboratory to correlate them to tephra layers deposited in distal records" - retrospective tephrostratigraphy for hazard assessment; the finalResults note that Turkish agencies "installed monitoring instruments on the active and dangerous Erciyes volcano", which is a third-party consequence, not an approach the project develops.
- 101025887 ENDGAME: "investigate transitions in eruptive styles at basaltic volcanoes through a combination of targeted, cutting-edge fluid dynamics experiments, a new holistic numerical model of magma ascent" - fragmentation process science; "hazard mitigation" only as downstream value.

Discrimination counter-examples (satisfy the text, fail the filter), from the unscoped pooled search plus a confirming SQL check of tag and countries:
- 798480 VOLCANOWAVES (tag yes, countries ES): "providing tools for a better and more accurate automatic volcano-seismic signals detection and classification to obtain Early Warning Decision Making algorithms... will improve our ability to forecast volcanic eruptions."
- 866085 DEEPVOLC (tag yes, countries UK): "The main deliverable will be a system for volcano observatories that uses knowledge of how volcanoes behave globally to automatically identify deformation at volcanoes locally, and forecast how the deformation will evolve, indicating the probability of eruption."
- 789887 TREMOR (tag yes, countries IS): "If TREMOR is successful, pre-eruptive tremor can be introduced as an eruption precursor, not only with direct application at IMO, but potentially worldwide."
- 101003173 MAST (tag yes, countries UK, CZ, FR): "The outputs will provide a scientific basis for observatories to interpret signals observed during unrest and to forecast future activity."
- 787399 SEISMAZE (tag yes, countries FR): "seismic tremors represent a unique source of information that can be used to... design new monitoring and forecasting approaches."

Scoped rank matrix (k=10, scope = the 15 survivors, index be84cbad9182), lexical/dense/hybrid/hybrid_rerank: PICVOLC 1/1/1/1, VULCAN.ears 7/2/2/2, SiC nano 2/6/4/3, ARISE2 8/3/6/4, EUROVOLC 3/4/3/6, IMPROVE 5/5/5/5, NEWTON-g 10/7/9/9, ChEESE 9/-/10/8; non-gold survivors surfacing: PUSKURUM 4/8/7/10, ENDGAME 6/9/8/7, ICELEARNING -/10/-/-.
why_good: This question discriminates on both axes at once: the country filter removes 47 of the 62 volcanology-tagged projects (including the strongest textual matches in the corpus - DEEPVOLC, VOLCANOWAVES, TREMOR, MAST, SEISMAZE), so a pure-vector condition retrieves confident but out-of-scope evidence, while a pure-SQL condition can only return 15 ids and cannot tell the 8 that build monitoring or forecasting capability from the 7 that do process science, data infrastructure or palaeo-reconstruction. It fills coverage axes not yet in the hybrid bank: a country/participant filter dimension (hyb-01 uses a date filter, hyb-03 a funding-percentile filter), an earth-sciences/volcanology topic branch, and the filter-survey subtype, which had no entry. The L3/filter-survey label is computed, not chosen: |gold| = 8 >= 5 with an exhaustive read of all 15 survivors, and exact-term is supported by the question's terms occurring verbatim in gold text and by four gold members ranking in the scoped lexical top-5.
checklist:
- ADJUDICATION-COMPLETE: PASS - S=15 (<=20), so every survivor was read (objective + report teaser for all 15; report summary + finalResults additionally for the four borderline cases 653980, 674907, 858092, 101025887) and each carries an IN/OUT reason in `notes`.
- FILTER-LOAD-BEARING: PASS - the unscoped pooled search on the same question surfaced five volcanology-tagged projects with no Italian participant that clearly satisfy the textual requirement (798480 VOLCANOWAVES ES, 866085 DEEPVOLC UK, 789887 TREMOR IS, 101003173 MAST UK/CZ/FR, 787399 SEISMAZE FR), and 47 of the 62 volcanology-tagged projects fail the country filter.
- TEXT-LOAD-BEARING: PASS - no column in `project`, `organization`, `euroscivoc` or `topics` records the monitoring/forecasting approach a project develops; the filter alone returns 15 ids and cannot separate the 8 that build such approaches from the 7 that do not.
- SUBTYPE-GOLD-BOUNDS: PASS - |gold| = 8, satisfying filter-survey's bound of >= 5 at L3.
- SCOPED-RETRIEVABLE: PASS - all 8 gold members appear in at least one condition's scoped top-10 (worst case ChEESE at hybrid_rerank 8 / lexical 9 / hybrid 10, absent only from dense).
- TERM-STYLE-HONEST: PASS - the question's terms ("volcanic unrest", "forecasting eruptions", "monitoring") occur verbatim in gold texts and four gold members rank in the scoped lexical top-5, which is what exact-term predicts.
- ONE-QUESTION: PASS - one filter (volcanology + Italian participant) plus one textual ask (what monitoring/forecasting approaches are developed); no second text ask.
- REFERENCE-FIDELITY: PASS - every claim in the reference traces to a quoted gold passage; acronyms (NEWTON-g, SiC nano for PicoGeo, VULCAN.ears, ARISE2, PICVOLC, IMPROVE, ChEESE, EUROVOLC), place names (Etna, Krafla, Nevado del Ruiz) and the "10-12" resolution figure are verbatim; no rejected survivor or out-of-filter project contributed.

findings.claim: The question scopes on 'volcanology projects with an Italian participating organisation', but gold is scoped on the euroSciVoc path %/volcanology%, which the question text never states. At least one project satisfies the question as asked and is excluded purely by that tag: DeepCube (101004188).
findings.evidence: Non-embedding sweep: projects with an IT organisation whose objective or title matches '%volcan%' but NOT in the volcanology-tagged set -> 11 rows. 101004188 DeepCube - objective 'UC4a: Automatic volcanic deformation detection and alerting'; report summary 'exploit the abundance of InSAR data to model ground deformation patterns of volcanic unrest'; finalResults name the Pluto system and a paper 'Self-Supervised Contrastive Learning for Volcanic Unrest Detection'. Organisation check: IT | TRE ALTAMIRA SRL | participant. Same profile as the drafter's own counter-example DEEPVOLC, except DeepCube passes the Italian-participant condition. Also 723986 EUNADICS-AV and 891467 ALARM (both IT-participating, untagged; ALARM ranked top-three in the critic's own-wording unscoped search, above several gold members). Crucially, the system under test cannot reproduce the tag scope: src/retrieval/scoped.py lines 57-67 restrict the id-narrowing filter to project/organization structured columns and state 'the subject matter / topic / research area of the question is NOT a structured filter' - euroSciVoc is not on that list, so the runtime scope for this question is organization.country='IT', inside which all three live and are semantically retrievable.
findings.fix_direction: Bounded text edit, no gold change: state the tag scope in the question as hyb-03 already does - 'Among Horizon 2020 projects classified under volcanology that have an Italian participating organisation, ...' - so the three become out-of-scope by the question's own words. The alternative (widening the filter and re-pooling) is a much larger re-derivation and would reopen F2.
findings.ruling_why: The critic executed a non-embedding sweep showing DeepCube (101004188, IT participant TRE ALTAMIRA SRL) develops project-owned 'volcanic unrest' detection and so satisfies the question exactly as worded, while being excluded only by an unstated euroSciVoc scope that src/retrieval/scoped.py provably cannot build (its filter whitelist is country/role/sme/dates/funding, not topic), so the gold set as recorded punishes a system that retrieves it - the brief's 'incomplete gold set that punishes the systems that did best'.

findings.claim: ARISE2 (653980) is a marginal gold member - it develops remote monitoring of erupting volcanoes and ash-plume/mass-eruption-rate prediction, not unrest monitoring or eruption forecasting. ChEESE (823844) sits on the same edge. They set the inclusion boundary wide enough to pull in the F1 projects.
findings.evidence: ARISE2's objective is a middle-atmosphere network project with volcanoes appearing once ('Among the applications, ARISE2 proposes infrasound remote volcano monitoring to provide notifications to civil aviation'); its finalResults claim is a Volcano Information System 'calibrated using Etna monitoring ... predict the ash plume height and mass eruption rate' - post-eruption plume products, not unrest precursors. ChEESE's volcano items are ash dispersal simulation and forecast, though its objective does carry 'data analysis and predictive techniques for earthquake and volcano monitoring', which the critic rates as making it the safer of the two. Contrast the unambiguous members: PICVOLC ('the source of volcanic unrest'), SiC nano ('strain transients preceding earthquakes and eruptions'), VULCAN.ears ('the main input used for eruption forecasting and early warning systems').
findings.fix_direction: Either accept the loose reading and treat F1 as the live issue, or narrow the question to the strict reading (e.g. 'approaches to detecting and interpreting pre-eruptive volcanic unrest'), which would drop ARISE2 and require re-checking ChEESE, taking gold to 6-7 (still L3). The critic notes the two routes are mutually exclusive and asks the judge to pick one.

record.text: Among the Marie Skłodowska-Curie individual fellowships classified under musicology, how do those trying to work out what ancient and prehistoric places sounded like to the people who used them go about it?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/musicology%' AND p.fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' ORDER BY p.id

record.reference_answer: Three of the 46 musicology-classified Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships do this - VRAASP, STESICHOROS and MEMORISING - and the step all three share is measuring how sound behaves at the sites themselves: VRAASP committed to fieldwork at 5 archaeological sites, which it does not name, and reports acoustic testing that explores the frequency spectrum and acoustic properties of the Hypogeum; STESICHOROS ran a fieldwork survey and field investigations of the linear theatre at Selinunte in Sicily plus an archaeoacoustics analysis giving the theatre's acoustic characteristics in their current state; MEMORISING documented rock art and the acoustics in the field, with test areas set out as the Montes de Prades (Tarragona, Spain) and Oaxaca (Mexico) and fieldwork reported at the Sierra de San Francisco in Baja California Sur and a 1km-deep cave in the Mixe region of Oaxaca. Past that shared step the three diverge. VRAASP and STESICHOROS carry the measurements into digital re-creation - VRAASP learned to use and acoustically analyse 3D models of archaeological sites and produced immersive, virtual reality (VR) and spectral representations of them, while STESICHOROS used 3D methods to reconstruct the theatre's size, shape and material structures and built an experimental interpretative 3D reconstruction integrating acoustic models, with auralisations of ancient instruments - whereas MEMORISING pairs its measurements with people instead, recording legends, traditions, stories, ritual activities and perceptions at the sites, interviews and ethnographic accounts, and collaborative work with the Ayuujk people of the Mixe region. The three also point the work at different questions: MEMORISING at the relationship between memory, rock art and acoustics and how knowledge was transmitted, VRAASP at the phenomenology and psychoacoustics of archaeological spaces and the sense of presence visitors feel in them, and STESICHOROS at why ancient cultures created such performative spaces and how they experienced them.

Gold project 750618 - VRAASP ("using Virtual Reality and Archaeoacoustic Analysis to Study and exhibit Presence", MSCA-IF-EF-ST). Objective, verbatim: "Unusual acoustic signatures of ancient or historical spaces, such as the West Kennet Long Barrow in England; caves in northern Spain containing prehistoric art; or Sculptor's Cave in Scotland, have captured the public imagination for centuries. ... Acousticians, composers, and acoustic archaeologists have studied acoustic phenomena, and archaeologists have compiled 3D models of archaeological sites for cultural preservation and exhibition purposes. The ER will use these technologies to engage in creative practice-led research on the phenomenology and acoustic archaeology of space. ... Throughout the fellowship, the ER will undertake field work at 5 archaeological sites, publish 1 paper and 1 studio report, present at 2 conferences, and organise a performance." Report summary: "The overall objectives were to create a toolkit, a set of processes, practices, methods, approaches, and skills, that could be used to explore sound presence. These have included skills in 3D modelling; interactive design; acoustic testing; acoustics analysis; acoustic modelling; musical composition ..."

Gold project 750706 - MEMORISING ("Remembering the Sound of Images: Cross-cultural study of rock art soundscapes and knowledge transmission in the New and Old Worlds.", MSCA-IF-EF-ST). Objective, verbatim: "The MEMORISING project will be a training-through-research project aiming to explore the relationships between memory, rock art and acoustics by using case studies from indigenous and non-indigenous backgrounds from Europe and America. ... I will record legends and traditions about the sites in Europe as well as stories, ritual activities and people's perceptions at sites in America. Following the methodology received in my training at the UB, I will test the acoustics of rock art sites in both areas. The importance of sound to present-day local communities in both regions will be explored through ways learned at the UB in the form of interviews, historical and ethnographic accounts. Test areas will be located in the Montes de Prades (Tarragona, Spain) and Oaxaca (Mexico)." Report workPerformed: "First at the intricate Sierra de San Francisco in Baja California Sur in Mexico (a World Heritage site with exceptional rock art) where access is only possible by mules, and at a unique 1km-deep cave in the Mixe region of Oaxaca. ... This study-case research speaks to questions regarding the methodology and the analysis of the placement of rock art in the landscape concerning sound."

Gold project 792058 - STESICHOROS ("THE ARCHAEOLOGY OF SOUND OF THE CULTIC THEATRE IN A GREEK CITY IN SICILY", MSCA-IF-EF-RI). Objective, verbatim: "Through this project I aim to assess and recover the lost intangible heritage of cultic theatre acoustics through the acoustic reconstruction of spaces of the past. ... The project will establish a new line of research at the crossroads of archaeomusicology, architecture, acoustics, and digital technologies to complete a study on these buildings, and will include a specific case study in Sicily. The acoustic reconstruction will also include audio material based on auralisations of ancient instruments." Report summary: "sound and performative space environments of the theatral step at Selinunte has been analysed and assessed. - To explore the reasons that led ancient cultures to create these spaces, as well as investigate how they experienced them by analysing both the physical acoustics and the way these acoustics shape what people perceive. - To model the relationship between intangible acoustic aspects (soundscapes) and the spatial configuration of ancient theatres ... to create an experimental interpretative 3D reconstruction integrating acoustic models".

Rejected survivors, reason-carrying ones quoted. 750086 Aural Paris - "This project examines the creative assimilation of the city of Paris into the music, film and literature of the French Third Republic (1870-1940)" - not an ancient or prehistoric place, no site acoustics. 101025090 MIKE-AGM - "Work on musical instruments involved studying published finds and studying key examples across a range of museums ... Work on iconography included compiling a catalogue of regional Greek black-figure vases" - ancient, but objects and repertoire, not how a place sounded. 101030908 MUSRES - "thousands of melodies ... remain hidden within the pages of palimpsest manuscripts" - manuscript recovery. 831852 MORPH - "Sound morphing has the potential to provide critical new insight into our understanding of timbre perception" - instrument timbre. record.text: Among Horizon 2020 projects classified under volcanology that have an Italian participating organisation, what approaches to monitoring volcanic unrest and forecasting eruptions are being developed?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id JOIN organization o ON o.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/volcanology%' AND o.country = 'IT' ORDER BY p.id

record.reference_answer: Eight of the fifteen Italian-participating volcanology projects develop such approaches, in three families. New instrumentation: NEWTON-g builds a field gravity imager - an array of low-cost MEMS relative gravimeters anchored on an absolute quantum gravimeter - deployed at Etna to image subsurface mass change continuously, while SiC nano for PicoGeo develops 3C-SiC optical nano-strain-meters (target resolution 10-12) to reveal the slow strain transients that precede eruptions, seeding a 'Pico strain Etna Lab'. Automated interpretation of monitoring signals: VULCAN.ears builds a volcano-independent automatic Volcano-Seismic Recognition system, based on structured Hidden Markov Models and a Parallel System Architecture, so observatories can classify precursory seismicity in real time, and ARISE2 turns its infrasound and lidar network into a Volcano Information System, calibrated using Etna monitoring, that estimates ash plume height and mass eruption rate remotely for aviation security. Modelling, imaging and shared infrastructure: PICVOLC jointly inverts seismic, gravity and deformation data with 3D Finite Element modelling to image the source of volcanic unrest at Nevado del Ruiz; IMPROVE images magma storage zones by combining seismic, geodetic, gravity and geochemical data with machine learning, and produced prototypes of advanced gas and steam monitoring devices as well as field-tested uses of fibre-optic sensing for volcano monitoring; ChEESE prepares exascale flagship codes for ensemble volcanic ash dispersal forecasting with satellite data assimilation and physics-based probabilistic volcanic hazard assessment; and EUROVOLC connects volcano observatories and research institutions, integrating modelling of pre-eruption data and virtual access to tools for responding to volcanic unrest and eruptions.
record.notes: FILTER: projects carrying a euroSciVoc path under volcanology (natural sciences/earth and related environmental sciences/geology/volcanology) that have at least one participating organisation in Italy (organization.country='IT', any role). Executed this pass: 15 survivors, against 62 projects carrying the volcanology tag overall, so 47 topic members fail the country filter. SCOPE STATED IN THE QUESTION: the question says 'classified under volcanology' because the euroSciVoc classification is an authoring scope the runtime scoped path cannot rebuild - src/retrieval/scoped.py whitelists only project/organization structured columns (country, role, dates, funding, scheme, sme, activityType) and excludes subject matter, so the scope it actually builds here is organization.country='IT'. Inside that wider scope there are Italian-participating projects that satisfy the textual ask but carry no volcanology tag - 101004188 DeepCube ('UC4a: Automatic volcanic deformation detection and alerting', InSAR modelling of 'ground deformation patterns of volcanic unrest'; Italian participant TRE ALTAMIRA SRL), 723986 EUNADICS-AV (near-real-time monitoring and data assimilation for airborne hazards including volcano eruptions) and 891467 ALARM (detection and nowcasting/forecasting of volcanic ash and SO2). Stating the classification in the question puts them out of scope as asked rather than leaving them as silent misses. ADJUDICATION (exhaustive, S=15 <= 20; every survivor's objective+teaser read, plus report summary/finalResults for the four borderline cases 653980, 674907, 858092, 101025887). IN: 653980 ARISE2 - final results report a Volcano Information System implemented on the ARISE infrasound platform, calibrated using Etna monitoring, for remote monitoring of non-instrumented volcanoes and prediction of ash plume height and mass eruption rate (marginal member: this is post-eruption plume characterisation rather than unrest monitoring or eruption forecasting); 731070 EUROVOLC - networks volcano observatories, integrated modelling of pre-eruption data and virtual access to tools for responding to volcanic unrest and eruptions; 749249 VULCAN.ears - automatic Volcano-Seismic Recognition system (structured HMMs + Parallel System Architecture) for real-time monitoring and eruption forecasting; 793811 PICVOLC - joint 3D numerical inversion of seismic, gravity and deformation data with FEM to image the source of volcanic unrest; 801221 NEWTON-g - MEMS/quantum gravimeter array as a field gravity imager for real-time monitoring of subsurface mass change at Etna; 823844 ChEESE - exascale codes for volcano monitoring, ensemble ash dispersal forecast with data assimilation, early-warning and physics-based hazard assessment; 858092 IMPROVE - subsurface imaging of magma systems plus fibre-optic sensing and gas/steam monitoring device prototypes, explicitly to enhance eruption forecasting; 863220 SiC nano for PicoGeo - 3C-SiC optical nano-strain-meters for detecting pre-eruptive strain transients, with a monitoring-network start-up at Etna. OUT: 658591 CIAO - petrology/geochemistry of Iranian ophiolite peridotites, no observation or forecasting method for active volcanoes; 674907 EVER-EST - generic Virtual Research Environment for Earth Science data and workflow preservation; its volcano/supersite use case consumes and shares data, it develops no monitoring or forecasting approach; 714936 TRUE DEPTHS - X-ray-diffraction elastic thermobarometry on UHP rocks to constrain subduction depths; 765710 INSIGHTS - statistics for particle physics, volcanology only as a secondment domain; 845115 ICELEARNING - AI classification of insoluble particles in ice cores (volcanic tephra as a particle class), a palaeoclimate analysis routine; 101024337 PUSKURUM - tephrostratigraphy of past Central Anatolian eruptions for retrospective hazard assessment, no monitoring or forecasting method developed (third parties installing instruments on Erciyes is a reported societal effect, not project work); 101025887 ENDGAME - shock-tube/jet-flow experiments and 3D magma-ascent modelling of basaltic fragmentation, process understanding rather than monitoring or forecasting capability. FILTER LOAD-BEARING: unscoped pooled search for the same question returns volcanology-tagged projects with no Italian participant that satisfy the textual requirement - 798480 VOLCANOWAVES (ES; automatic volcano-seismic detection for eruption forecast modelling), 866085 DEEPVOLC (UK; deep learning on Sentinel-1 deformation to forecast volcanic activity), 789887 TREMOR (IS; pre-eruptive tremor as an eruption precursor), 101003173 MAST (UK/CZ/FR; strain tomography of volcano deformation to interpret unrest signals), 787399 SEISMAZE (FR; tremor analysis for new monitoring and forecasting approaches). Verified by SQL that each carries the volcanology tag and has no IT organisation. TEXT LOAD-BEARING: no stored column records what monitoring or forecasting approach a project develops; the answer exists only in objective and report free text. RETRIEVABILITY: scoped pooled search (k=10 over the 15 survivors) ranks all eight gold members in at least one condition's top-10 (PICVOLC 1/1/1/1, VULCAN.ears 7/2/2/2, SiC nano 2/6/4/3, ARISE2 8/3/6/4, EUROVOLC 3/4/3/6, IMPROVE 5/5/5/5, NEWTON-g 10/7/9/9, ChEESE 9/-/10/8 as lexical/dense/hybrid/hybrid_rerank). TERM_STYLE exact-term: the question reuses vocabulary present verbatim in gold texts - 'volcanic unrest' (PICVOLC, EUROVOLC), 'eruption forecasting' / 'forecasting volcanic eruptions' (VULCAN.ears, SiC nano), 'volcano monitoring' (ARISE2, ChEESE, IMPROVE); consistent with strong lexical ranks for four gold members. Adjudication came from the exhaustive read; the scoped pooled search supplied pooled_candidate_count (11 of the 15 survivors surfaced) and the rank matrix only.

evidence:
Filter (executed this pass, true survivor count 15, <= 200):
SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p
JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id
JOIN organization o ON o.projectID = p.id
WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/volcanology%' AND o.country = 'IT'
ORDER BY p.id
-> 15 survivors: 653980 ARISE2, 658591 CIAO, 674907 EVER-EST, 714936 TRUE DEPTHS, 731070 EUROVOLC, 749249 VULCAN.ears, 765710 INSIGHTS, 793811 PICVOLC, 801221 NEWTON-g, 823844 ChEESE, 845115 ICELEARNING, 858092 IMPROVE, 863220 SiC nano for PicoGeo, 101024337 PUSKURUM, 101025887 ENDGAME.
Topic total without the country condition: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT projectID) FROM euroscivoc WHERE euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/volcanology%' -> 62, i.e. 47 topic members are removed by the Italian-participant condition.

Gold members, with the passages that satisfy the question (verbatim):

653980 ARISE2 - report finalResults: "The Volcano Information System (VIS) implemented in the ARISE platform and presently calibrated using Etna monitoring will be very relevant for remote monitoring of non-instrumented volcanoes. The ARISE team demonstrated the possibility to predict the ash plume height and mass eruption rate based on the infrasound signals associated to the eruptions with a large impact for the aviation security." Objective: "ARISE2 proposes infrasound remote volcano monitoring to provide notifications to civil aviation."

731070 EUROVOLC - objective: "Joint research activities include production of services to initialize volcanic ash transport and dispersal models during eruptions, integrated modelling of pre-eruption data, and a complete catalogue of European Volcanoes. Trans-national access to European Volcano observatories will be facilitated and virtual access to various modelling and assessment tools for responding to volcanic unrest and eruptions will be offered."

749249 VULCAN.ears - objective: "The aim of this proposal is to build an automatic VSR system focused on recognising events in unsupervised scenarios, robust enough to be integrated into the VM centre of any volcano, allowing online risk assessment by real-time seismicity analysis. It will be based on state-of-the-art VSR technologies: a) class description by statistical means (structured Hidden Markov Models) and b) Parallel System Architecture (PSA-VSR) composed of specialised recognition channels"; report summary: "the main input used for eruption forecasting and early warning systems."

793811 PICVOLC - objective: "PICVOLC aims to overcome the limitations in the current approach in the modeling of volcanic unrest by developing a new, original methodology that integrates seismic, gravity, and deformation data with 3D numerical inversion to create a detailed representation of the source of volcanic unrest... PICVOLC involves the integration of fieldwork with Finite Element Methods modeling and joint numerical inversions of geodetic and geophysical data."

801221 NEWTON-g - objective: "We aim at developing a field-compatible gravity imager able to real-time monitor the evolution of the subsurface mass changes through continuous images of the gravity field. This system will include an array of low-costs MEMS-based relative gravimeters anchored on an absolute quantum gravimeter... We will deploy the new gravity imager at Etna volcano (Italy)"; finalResults: "NEWTON-g will thus help to take a step forward in volcano monitoring, through opening a new window for hazard assessment."

823844 ChEESE - objective: "data analysis and predictive techniques for earthquake and volcano monitoring... ensemble-based volcanic ash dispersal, faster than real-time tsunami simulations and physics-based hazard assessments for seismics, volcanoes and tsunamis"; finalResults: "High-resolution volcanic ash dispersal simulations for hazard assessment and operational forecast using data assimilation (ECC8)... Volcanic ash dispersal forecasts at unprecedented resolution (few km) based on satellite data assimilation and ensemble forecast."

858092 IMPROVE - report summary: "It produced new methods to image magma storage zones and to link seismic, geodetic, and geochemical observations across scales. It also created prototypes for advanced gas and steam monitoring devices, demonstrated new uses of fibre-optic sensing for volcano monitoring"; finalResults: "IMPROVE pioneered new techniques for subsurface imaging, combining seismic, geodetic, gravity, and geochemical data with machine learning and numerical modelling... Improved understanding of subsurface processes directly enhances eruption forecasting and volcanic hazard assessment."

863220 SiC nano for PicoGeo - objective: "The goal is the development of a radically new dynamic ground strain measurement technology with an ultra-high resolution of 10-12... Ultra small and slow strain transients preceding earthquakes and eruptions could be revealed... the project outcomes will have direct implications in forecasting volcanic eruptions and thus improve volcano-seismic crisis management. At the end of the project a start-up of one innovative frontier laboratory for advanced monitoring of dynamic strain associated to volcanic and seismic processes will be done. This 'Pico strain Etna Lab' will be the starting point of a new network infrastructure".

Survivors adjudicated OUT (7), with the text that decides them:
- 658591 CIAO: "CIAO will study the amphibole-bearing peridotites of Nain ophiolite (Iran)... measuring major, trace and volatile element concentrations" - laboratory petrology; volcano hazards only as a distant hope ("hoping to reduce the hazards"). No monitoring or forecasting approach.
- 674907 EVER-EST: "developing a generic Virtual Research Environment (VRE) providing earth scientists with the means to manage both the data involved in their disciplines and the scientific methods applied in their observations" - data/workflow infrastructure; the volcano-related use cases are user communities ("disaster and risk management teams (Supersites use case)"), not an approach the project develops.
- 714936 TRUE DEPTHS: "will develop X-ray diffraction analysis of the anisotropic elastic interactions of inclusion minerals trapped inside host minerals" to determine subduction depths - no volcano observation or forecasting.
- 765710 INSIGHTS: "develop advanced statistical methods... to solve problems in Particle Physics"; volcanology appears only as a secondment field ("secondments with partners in other disciplines such as Finance, Climate Science and Volcanology").
- 845115 ICELEARNING: "a two-phase routine for the automatic quantification of insoluble particles trapped in ice cores" - tephra is one particle class in a palaeoclimate routine; no volcano monitoring.
- 101024337 PUSKURUM: "their chemical composition and eruption ages will be determined in the laboratory to correlate them to tephra layers deposited in distal records" - retrospective tephrostratigraphy for hazard assessment; the finalResults note that Turkish agencies "installed monitoring instruments on the active and dangerous Erciyes volcano", which is a third-party consequence, not an approach the project develops.
- 101025887 ENDGAME: "investigate transitions in eruptive styles at basaltic volcanoes through a combination of targeted, cutting-edge fluid dynamics experiments, a new holistic numerical model of magma ascent" - fragmentation process science; "hazard mitigation" only as downstream value.

Discrimination counter-examples (satisfy the text, fail the filter), from the unscoped pooled search plus a confirming SQL check of tag and countries:
- 798480 VOLCANOWAVES (tag yes, countries ES): "providing tools for a better and more accurate automatic volcano-seismic signals detection and classification to obtain Early Warning Decision Making algorithms... will improve our ability to forecast volcanic eruptions."
- 866085 DEEPVOLC (tag yes, countries UK): "The main deliverable will be a system for volcano observatories that uses knowledge of how volcanoes behave globally to automatically identify deformation at volcanoes locally, and forecast how the deformation will evolve, indicating the probability of eruption."
- 789887 TREMOR (tag yes, countries IS): "If TREMOR is successful, pre-eruptive tremor can be introduced as an eruption precursor, not only with direct application at IMO, but potentially worldwide."
- 101003173 MAST (tag yes, countries UK, CZ, FR): "The outputs will provide a scientific basis for observatories to interpret signals observed during unrest and to forecast future activity."
- 787399 SEISMAZE (tag yes, countries FR): "seismic tremors represent a unique source of information that can be used to... design new monitoring and forecasting approaches."

Scoped rank matrix (k=10, scope = the 15 survivors, index be84cbad9182), lexical/dense/hybrid/hybrid_rerank: PICVOLC 1/1/1/1, VULCAN.ears 7/2/2/2, SiC nano 2/6/4/3, ARISE2 8/3/6/4, EUROVOLC 3/4/3/6, IMPROVE 5/5/5/5, NEWTON-g 10/7/9/9, ChEESE 9/-/10/8; non-gold survivors surfacing: PUSKURUM 4/8/7/10, ENDGAME 6/9/8/7, ICELEARNING -/10/-/-.

--- ROUND 2 ---

Untagged Italian-participating satisfiers, now excluded by the question's stated classification (the critic's HIGH finding, recorded in the record's notes so a promote-time reader can see exactly what the stated scope excludes and why): 101004188 DeepCube ("UC4a: Automatic volcanic deformation detection and alerting"; InSAR modelling of "ground deformation patterns of volcanic unrest"; Italian participant TRE ALTAMIRA SRL, role participant), 723986 EUNADICS-AV (near-real-time monitoring and data assimilation for airborne hazards including volcano eruptions), 891467 ALARM (detection and nowcasting/forecasting of volcanic ash and SO2). None carries a euroSciVoc volcanology path, so none is a survivor of filter_sql.

IMPROVE reference clause, tightened (the round-1 LOW, taken voluntarily): the clause no longer attributes the prototypes to a site. record.text: Among the Marie Skłodowska-Curie individual fellowships classified under musicology, how do those trying to work out what ancient and prehistoric places sounded like to the people who used them go about it?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/musicology%' AND p.fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' ORDER BY p.id

record.reference_answer: Three of the 46 musicology-classified Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships do this - VRAASP, STESICHOROS and MEMORISING - and the step all three share is measuring how sound behaves at the sites themselves: VRAASP committed to fieldwork at 5 archaeological sites, which it does not name, and reports acoustic testing that explores the frequency spectrum and acoustic properties of the Hypogeum; STESICHOROS ran a fieldwork survey and field investigations of the linear theatre at Selinunte in Sicily plus an archaeoacoustics analysis giving the theatre's acoustic characteristics in their current state; MEMORISING documented rock art and the acoustics in the field, with test areas set out as the Montes de Prades (Tarragona, Spain) and Oaxaca (Mexico) and fieldwork reported at the Sierra de San Francisco in Baja California Sur and a 1km-deep cave in the Mixe region of Oaxaca. Past that shared step the three diverge. VRAASP and STESICHOROS carry the measurements into digital re-creation - VRAASP learned to use and acoustically analyse 3D models of archaeological sites and produced immersive, virtual reality (VR) and spectral representations of them, while STESICHOROS used 3D methods to reconstruct the theatre's size, shape and material structures and built an experimental interpretative 3D reconstruction integrating acoustic models, with auralisations of ancient instruments - whereas MEMORISING pairs its measurements with people instead, recording legends, traditions, stories, ritual activities and perceptions at the sites, interviews and ethnographic accounts, and collaborative work with the Ayuujk people of the Mixe region. The three also point the work at different questions: MEMORISING at the relationship between memory, rock art and acoustics and how knowledge was transmitted, VRAASP at the phenomenology and psychoacoustics of archaeological spaces and the sense of presence visitors feel in them, and STESICHOROS at why ancient cultures created such performative spaces and how they experienced them.
record.notes: FILTER: euroSciVoc path containing '/musicology' AND fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' -> 46 survivors (executed this pass, row_count 46, <= 200 so enumerable). Scheme half is stated in user language as 'Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships'; the six MSCA-IF* codes present in the survivor set are MSCA-IF (26), MSCA-IF-EF-ST (13), MSCA-IF-GF (3), MSCA-IF-EF-CAR (2), MSCA-IF-EF-RI (1), MSCA-IF-EF-SE (1), all of them Individual Fellowships, and the LIKE excludes MSCA-RISE (staff exchange, 1 musicology project). Musicology overall has 86 projects; the scheme half removes 40 of them (ERC-ADG 10, SME-1 9, ERC-COG 6, SME-2 4, IA 3, RIA 3, ERC-POC 3, ERC-STG 1, MSCA-RISE 1). The candidate seed's narrower filter fundingScheme='MSCA-IF-EF-ST' (13 survivors) was rejected: that bare scheme code is not something a user would state, and it would arbitrarily drop MSCA-IF-GF/CAR/RI/SE fellowships that are equally 'individual fellowships'; the broader family filter is the user-expressible version and was re-executed this pass. ADJUDICATION (S=46 > 20, so the scoped-pooled + survivor-sweep protocol was run, not an exhaustive read): (1) scoped pooled search with the final question text over all 46 survivors returned 20 distinct projects; (2) two SQL keyword sweeps over ALL 46 survivors' objective + report teaser/summary (and a second over objective + all report sections) on acoustic / soundscape / archaeolog / archaeo / ancient / prehistor / antiquity / reverberat / cave / temple / excavat / ruin / rock art / resonanc / megalith / neolithic / bce / aurali flagged only 750618, 750706, 792058, 750086, 831852, 101025090, 101030908, 706016, 745631 - the union of the two channels was adjudicated. IN: 750618 VRAASP (fieldwork at 5 archaeological sites, acoustic signatures of ancient/historical spaces, 3D+VR modelling), 750706 MEMORISING (tests the acoustics of rock art sites in Spain and Mexico plus ethnographic interviews), 792058 STESICHOROS (acoustic reconstruction of the cultic theatre/theatral step at Selinunte, 3D models and auralisations). OUT with reason: 750086 Aural Paris (creative responses to the sounds of Paris 1870-1940 in music/film/literature - not an ancient or prehistoric place and no site acoustics); 101025090 MIKE-AGM (Archaic Greek music via instruments, pottery iconography and texts - ancient, but studies objects and repertoire, not how a place sounded); 101030908 MUSRES (recovers chant erased from medieval palimpsest manuscripts - textual recovery, no place); 831852 MORPH (timbre morphing of musical instrument sounds - 'acoustic' hit only); 706016 MUSDEWAR (music in Greek detention camps 1947-1957); 745631 GRIDAMUS (Greek art music since 1830, 'antiquity' hit only); plus the remaining scoped-pooled hits, all clearly off-theme from their best chunk: 844238 ClassRockED, 661385 ICH-Bildung, 890285 MusiConduits, 101029971 Harmony on the Edge, 101027258 WOMENSONG, 659468 Transnational Localism, 701269 GoldOpera, 792150 LadinoProverbs, 894071 REWID, 101020153 COMPHIL, 101030595 ARPOEXMUS, 101038090 RESALVE. FILTER DISCRIMINATION (unscoped pooled search with the same question, plus a corpus-wide SQL sweep for archaeoacoustics wording): 787842 ARTSOUNDSCAPES ('The sound of special places: exploring rock art soundscapes and the sacred', ERC-ADG, tagged visual arts + archaeology) satisfies the textual ask outright and fails both halves of the filter - it was the top hit in all four conditions on a bare textual phrasing of the ask and still ranks dense 2 / hybrid 3 / hybrid_rerank 8 on the full question; 846012 TVSM (MSCA-IF, 'Teotihuacan Virtual Sound Map', tagged ancient history + acoustics) recreates the sonic sphere of a pre-Columbian city and fails only the musicology half; 897905 ACOUSTIC ATLAS (MSCA-IF, tagged ecology + acoustics) captures and auralises the acoustics of Dowkerbottom and Ingleborough Caves; 797586 CATHEDRAL ACOUSTICS (MSCA-IF-EF-ST, tagged history + acoustics) measures and virtually recreates English cathedral acoustics through history. So the filter is load-bearing: an unfiltered topical search returns satisfying projects that are not gold. Within the 86 musicology-tagged projects, no non-MSCA-IF project satisfies the textual ask (checked by the same keyword sweep over the 40 non-MSCA-IF musicology projects: DTHPS, DoReMIR, CoHERE, IRiMaS, DIDONE, DigiScore, MUTE were the only keyword hits and none studies the acoustics of a past place), so the scheme half narrows the survivor set without removing a text-satisfier. TEXT LOAD-BEARING: no stored column records what a project investigates; the answer comes from objectives and report summaries. TERM_STYLE: paraphrase - the question avoids every distinctive term the gold texts use (archaeoacoustics, acoustics, acoustic signature, soundscape, rock art, cultic theatre, auralisation, resonance, presence, phenomenology) and asks in plain words. Scoped rank matrix on the final text: VRAASP lexical 2 / dense 2 / hybrid 1 / rerank 1; STESICHOROS lexical 3 / dense 1 / hybrid 2 / rerank 4; MEMORISING lexical null / dense 3 / hybrid 4 / rerank 5 - lexical does reach two of the three gold on shared everyday words (sound, ancient, prehistoric, places, people), which is recorded here rather than argued away. Gold project 750618 - VRAASP ("using Virtual Reality and Archaeoacoustic Analysis to Study and exhibit Presence", MSCA-IF-EF-ST). Objective, verbatim: "Unusual acoustic signatures of ancient or historical spaces, such as the West Kennet Long Barrow in England; caves in northern Spain containing prehistoric art; or Sculptor's Cave in Scotland, have captured the public imagination for centuries. ... Acousticians, composers, and acoustic archaeologists have studied acoustic phenomena, and archaeologists have compiled 3D models of archaeological sites for cultural preservation and exhibition purposes. The ER will use these technologies to engage in creative practice-led research on the phenomenology and acoustic archaeology of space. ... Throughout the fellowship, the ER will undertake field work at 5 archaeological sites, publish 1 paper and 1 studio report, present at 2 conferences, and organise a performance." Report summary: "The overall objectives were to create a toolkit, a set of processes, practices, methods, approaches, and skills, that could be used to explore sound presence. These have included skills in 3D modelling; interactive design; acoustic testing; acoustics analysis; acoustic modelling; musical composition ..."

Gold project 750706 - MEMORISING ("Remembering the Sound of Images: Cross-cultural study of rock art soundscapes and knowledge transmission in the New and Old Worlds.", MSCA-IF-EF-ST). Objective, verbatim: "The MEMORISING project will be a training-through-research project aiming to explore the relationships between memory, rock art and acoustics by using case studies from indigenous and non-indigenous backgrounds from Europe and America. ... I will record legends and traditions about the sites in Europe as well as stories, ritual activities and people's perceptions at sites in America. Following the methodology received in my training at the UB, I will test the acoustics of rock art sites in both areas. The importance of sound to present-day local communities in both regions will be explored through ways learned at the UB in the form of interviews, historical and ethnographic accounts. Test areas will be located in the Montes de Prades (Tarragona, Spain) and Oaxaca (Mexico)." Report workPerformed: "First at the intricate Sierra de San Francisco in Baja California Sur in Mexico (a World Heritage site with exceptional rock art) where access is only possible by mules, and at a unique 1km-deep cave in the Mixe region of Oaxaca. ... This study-case research speaks to questions regarding the methodology and the analysis of the placement of rock art in the landscape concerning sound."

Gold project 792058 - STESICHOROS ("THE ARCHAEOLOGY OF SOUND OF THE CULTIC THEATRE IN A GREEK CITY IN SICILY", MSCA-IF-EF-RI). Objective, verbatim: "Through this project I aim to assess and recover the lost intangible heritage of cultic theatre acoustics through the acoustic reconstruction of spaces of the past. ... The project will establish a new line of research at the crossroads of archaeomusicology, architecture, acoustics, and digital technologies to complete a study on these buildings, and will include a specific case study in Sicily. The acoustic reconstruction will also include audio material based on auralisations of ancient instruments." Report summary: "sound and performative space environments of the theatral step at Selinunte has been analysed and assessed. - To explore the reasons that led ancient cultures to create these spaces, as well as investigate how they experienced them by analysing both the physical acoustics and the way these acoustics shape what people perceive. - To model the relationship between intangible acoustic aspects (soundscapes) and the spatial configuration of ancient theatres ... to create an experimental interpretative 3D reconstruction integrating acoustic models".

Rejected survivors, reason-carrying ones quoted. 750086 Aural Paris - "This project examines the creative assimilation of the city of Paris into the music, film and literature of the French Third Republic (1870-1940)" - not an ancient or prehistoric place, no site acoustics. 101025090 MIKE-AGM - "Work on musical instruments involved studying published finds and studying key examples across a range of museums ... This candidate's single fix round is already spent, so there is no round in which to reword the filter half; the candidate is abandoned with an UPHELD HIGH outstanding rather than accepted with it. record.text: Among Horizon 2020 projects classified under volcanology that have an Italian participating organisation, what approaches to monitoring volcanic unrest and forecasting eruptions are being developed?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id JOIN organization o ON o.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/volcanology%' AND o.country = 'IT' ORDER BY p.id

record.reference_answer: Eight of the fifteen Italian-participating volcanology projects develop such approaches, in three families. New instrumentation: NEWTON-g builds a field gravity imager - an array of low-cost MEMS relative gravimeters anchored on an absolute quantum gravimeter - deployed at Etna to image subsurface mass change continuously, while SiC nano for PicoGeo develops 3C-SiC optical nano-strain-meters (target resolution 10-12) to reveal the slow strain transients that precede eruptions, seeding a 'Pico strain Etna Lab'. Automated interpretation of monitoring signals: VULCAN.ears builds a volcano-independent automatic Volcano-Seismic Recognition system, based on structured Hidden Markov Models and a Parallel System Architecture, so observatories can classify precursory seismicity in real time, and ARISE2 turns its infrasound and lidar network into a Volcano Information System, calibrated using Etna monitoring, that estimates ash plume height and mass eruption rate remotely for aviation security. Modelling, imaging and shared infrastructure: PICVOLC jointly inverts seismic, gravity and deformation data with 3D Finite Element modelling to image the source of volcanic unrest at Nevado del Ruiz; IMPROVE images magma storage zones by combining seismic, geodetic, gravity and geochemical data with machine learning, and produced prototypes of advanced gas and steam monitoring devices as well as field-tested uses of fibre-optic sensing for volcano monitoring; ChEESE prepares exascale flagship codes for ensemble volcanic ash dispersal forecasting with satellite data assimilation and physics-based probabilistic volcanic hazard assessment; and EUROVOLC connects volcano observatories and research institutions, integrating modelling of pre-eruption data and virtual access to tools for responding to volcanic unrest and eruptions.
record.notes: FILTER: projects carrying a euroSciVoc path under volcanology (natural sciences/earth and related environmental sciences/geology/volcanology) that have at least one participating organisation in Italy (organization.country='IT', any role). Executed this pass: 15 survivors, against 62 projects carrying the volcanology tag overall, so 47 topic members fail the country filter. SCOPE STATED IN THE QUESTION: the question says 'classified under volcanology' because the euroSciVoc classification is an authoring scope the runtime scoped path cannot rebuild - src/retrieval/scoped.py whitelists only project/organization structured columns (country, role, dates, funding, scheme, sme, activityType) and excludes subject matter, so the scope it actually builds here is organization.country='IT'. Inside that wider scope there are Italian-participating projects that satisfy the textual ask but carry no volcanology tag - 101004188 DeepCube ('UC4a: Automatic volcanic deformation detection and alerting', InSAR modelling of 'ground deformation patterns of volcanic unrest'; Italian participant TRE ALTAMIRA SRL), 723986 EUNADICS-AV (near-real-time monitoring and data assimilation for airborne hazards including volcano eruptions) and 891467 ALARM (detection and nowcasting/forecasting of volcanic ash and SO2). Stating the classification in the question puts them out of scope as asked rather than leaving them as silent misses. ADJUDICATION (exhaustive, S=15 <= 20; every survivor's objective+teaser read, plus report summary/finalResults for the four borderline cases 653980, 674907, 858092, 101025887). IN: 653980 ARISE2 - final results report a Volcano Information System implemented on the ARISE infrasound platform, calibrated using Etna monitoring, for remote monitoring of non-instrumented volcanoes and prediction of ash plume height and mass eruption rate (marginal member: this is post-eruption plume characterisation rather than unrest monitoring or eruption forecasting); 731070 EUROVOLC - networks volcano observatories, integrated modelling of pre-eruption data and virtual access to tools for responding to volcanic unrest and eruptions; 749249 VULCAN.ears - automatic Volcano-Seismic Recognition system (structured HMMs + Parallel System Architecture) for real-time monitoring and eruption forecasting; 793811 PICVOLC - joint 3D numerical inversion of seismic, gravity and deformation data with FEM to image the source of volcanic unrest; 801221 NEWTON-g - MEMS/quantum gravimeter array as a field gravity imager for real-time monitoring of subsurface mass change at Etna; 823844 ChEESE - exascale codes for volcano monitoring, ensemble ash dispersal forecast with data assimilation, early-warning and physics-based hazard assessment; 858092 IMPROVE - subsurface imaging of magma systems plus fibre-optic sensing and gas/steam monitoring device prototypes, explicitly to enhance eruption forecasting; 863220 SiC nano for PicoGeo - 3C-SiC optical nano-strain-meters for detecting pre-eruptive strain transients, with a monitoring-network start-up at Etna. OUT: 658591 CIAO - petrology/geochemistry of Iranian ophiolite peridotites, no observation or forecasting method for active volcanoes; 674907 EVER-EST - generic Virtual Research Environment for Earth Science data and workflow preservation; its volcano/supersite use case consumes and shares data, it develops no monitoring or forecasting approach; 714936 TRUE DEPTHS - X-ray-diffraction elastic thermobarometry on UHP rocks to constrain subduction depths; 765710 INSIGHTS - statistics for particle physics, volcanology only as a secondment domain; 845115 ICELEARNING - AI classification of insoluble particles in ice cores (volcanic tephra as a particle class), a palaeoclimate analysis routine; 101024337 PUSKURUM - tephrostratigraphy of past Central Anatolian eruptions for retrospective hazard assessment, no monitoring or forecasting method developed (third parties installing instruments on Erciyes is a reported societal effect, not project work); 101025887 ENDGAME - shock-tube/jet-flow experiments and 3D magma-ascent modelling of basaltic fragmentation, process understanding rather than monitoring or forecasting capability. FILTER LOAD-BEARING: unscoped pooled search for the same question returns volcanology-tagged projects with no Italian participant that satisfy the textual requirement - 798480 VOLCANOWAVES (ES; automatic volcano-seismic detection for eruption forecast modelling), 866085 DEEPVOLC (UK; deep learning on Sentinel-1 deformation to forecast volcanic activity), 789887 TREMOR (IS; pre-eruptive tremor as an eruption precursor), 101003173 MAST (UK/CZ/FR; strain tomography of volcano deformation to interpret unrest signals), 787399 SEISMAZE (FR; tremor analysis for new monitoring and forecasting approaches). Verified by SQL that each carries the volcanology tag and has no IT organisation. TEXT LOAD-BEARING: no stored column records what monitoring or forecasting approach a project develops; the answer exists only in objective and report free text. RETRIEVABILITY: scoped pooled search (k=10 over the 15 survivors) ranks all eight gold members in at least one condition's top-10 (PICVOLC 1/1/1/1, VULCAN.ears 7/2/2/2, SiC nano 2/6/4/3, ARISE2 8/3/6/4, EUROVOLC 3/4/3/6, IMPROVE 5/5/5/5, NEWTON-g 10/7/9/9, ChEESE 9/-/10/8 as lexical/dense/hybrid/hybrid_rerank). TERM_STYLE exact-term: the question reuses vocabulary present verbatim in gold texts - 'volcanic unrest' (PICVOLC, EUROVOLC), 'eruption forecasting' / 'forecasting volcanic eruptions' (VULCAN.ears, SiC nano), 'volcano monitoring' (ARISE2, ChEESE, IMPROVE); consistent with strong lexical ranks for four gold members. Adjudication came from the exhaustive read; the scoped pooled search supplied pooled_candidate_count (11 of the 15 survivors surfaced) and the rank matrix only.

PICVOLC involves the integration of fieldwork with Finite Element Methods modeling and joint numerical inversions of geodetic and geophysical data."

801221 NEWTON-g - objective: "We aim at developing a field-compatible gravity imager able to real-time monitor the evolution of the subsurface mass changes through continuous images of the gravity field. 858092 IMPROVE - report summary: "It produced new methods to image magma storage zones and to link seismic, geodetic, and geochemical observations across scales. At the end of the project a start-up of one innovative frontier laboratory for advanced monitoring of dynamic strain associated to volcanic and seismic processes will be done. record.text: Among Horizon 2020 projects classified under volcanology that have an Italian participating organisation, what approaches to monitoring volcanic unrest and forecasting eruptions are being developed?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id JOIN organization o ON o.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/volcanology%' AND o.country = 'IT' ORDER BY p.id

record.reference_answer: Eight of the fifteen Italian-participating volcanology projects develop such approaches, in three families. New instrumentation: NEWTON-g builds a field gravity imager - an array of low-cost MEMS relative gravimeters anchored on an absolute quantum gravimeter - deployed at Etna to image subsurface mass change continuously, while SiC nano for PicoGeo develops 3C-SiC optical nano-strain-meters (target resolution 10-12) to reveal the slow strain transients that precede eruptions, seeding a 'Pico strain Etna Lab'. Automated interpretation of monitoring signals: VULCAN.ears builds a volcano-independent automatic Volcano-Seismic Recognition system, based on structured Hidden Markov Models and a Parallel System Architecture, so observatories can classify precursory seismicity in real time, and ARISE2 turns its infrasound and lidar network into a Volcano Information System, calibrated using Etna monitoring, that estimates ash plume height and mass eruption rate remotely for aviation security. Modelling, imaging and shared infrastructure: PICVOLC jointly inverts seismic, gravity and deformation data with 3D Finite Element modelling to image the source of volcanic unrest at Nevado del Ruiz; IMPROVE images magma storage zones by combining seismic, geodetic, gravity and geochemical data with machine learning, and produced prototypes of advanced gas and steam monitoring devices as well as field-tested uses of fibre-optic sensing for volcano monitoring; ChEESE prepares exascale flagship codes for ensemble volcanic ash dispersal forecasting with satellite data assimilation and physics-based probabilistic volcanic hazard assessment; and EUROVOLC connects volcano observatories and research institutions, integrating modelling of pre-eruption data and virtual access to tools for responding to volcanic unrest and eruptions.
record.notes: FILTER: projects carrying a euroSciVoc path under volcanology (natural sciences/earth and related environmental sciences/geology/volcanology) that have at least one participating organisation in Italy (organization.country='IT', any role). Executed this pass: 15 survivors, against 62 projects carrying the volcanology tag overall, so 47 topic members fail the country filter. SCOPE STATED IN THE QUESTION: the question says 'classified under volcanology' because the euroSciVoc classification is an authoring scope the runtime scoped path cannot rebuild - src/retrieval/scoped.py whitelists only project/organization structured columns (country, role, dates, funding, scheme, sme, activityType) and excludes subject matter, so the scope it actually builds here is organization.country='IT'. Inside that wider scope there are Italian-participating projects that satisfy the textual ask but carry no volcanology tag - 101004188 DeepCube ('UC4a: Automatic volcanic deformation detection and alerting', InSAR modelling of 'ground deformation patterns of volcanic unrest'; Italian participant TRE ALTAMIRA SRL), 723986 EUNADICS-AV (near-real-time monitoring and data assimilation for airborne hazards including volcano eruptions) and 891467 ALARM (detection and nowcasting/forecasting of volcanic ash and SO2). Stating the classification in the question puts them out of scope as asked rather than leaving them as silent misses. judge_decisions.rationale: The cell is supposed to measure whether scoped retrieval can survey a filtered topical set, but as worded the question states a scope (Italian participant + 'volcanology projects') strictly wider than the scope the gold was derived from (the euroSciVoc tag), so a system that correctly surfaces DeepCube's volcanic-unrest work is scored as adding unsupported material - a wrong finding, not a wrong answer. The bounded repair is to state the tag scope in the question, matching the promoted-bank precedent of hyb-03, leaving gold, level, survivors and filter evidence untouched. The judge deliberately did NOT take the critic's alternative route of narrowing the topic to strict pre-eruptive unrest: the critic itself says the two routes are mutually exclusive, and that one re-derives gold rather than repairing scope. record.text: Among the SME Instrument phase 1 projects classified under viticulture, how do the ones that build on a producer's own naturally occurring organisms, rather than on bought-in standard cultures, put those organisms to work in making wine?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocTitle = 'viticulture' AND p.fundingScheme = 'SME-1' ORDER BY p.id

record.reference_answer: Two of the 14 SME Instrument phase 1 projects tagged viticulture take this route, and both make the producer's own resident biology the source of a wine competitors cannot replicate. MYBIOASSET (LEV2050) treats a winery's own bio-imprint as a commercial asset: it genetically selects, preserves and reproduces indigenous yeasts of different strains, so a house can keep dependable, robust fermentation and still bottle singular wines, the firm's stated aim being to recover the old diversity of wines without giving up modern production technology. Eternum works from the vineyard outwards: Bodegas Langa, with 150 years of winemaking expertise, profiles the vineyard's own microbiology and uses that profile both to draw up a highly specific low-impact pest control plan and to pick the site's own fermentation yeasts, then matures the wine together with those yeasts in a purpose-designed container that mimics the shape of a maturation deposit, so nutrients the organisms yield keep enriching the wine inside the bottle. The shared move is to replace a bought-in standardised input with an on-site biological one, LEV2050 packaging it as a technology any winery can buy and Bodegas Langa applying it to its own estate's production.

record.text: Among the SME Instrument phase 1 projects classified under viticulture, how do the ones that build on a producer's own naturally occurring organisms, rather than on bought-in standard cultures, put those organisms to work in making wine?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocTitle = 'viticulture' AND p.fundingScheme = 'SME-1' ORDER BY p.id

record.reference_answer: Two of the 14 SME Instrument phase 1 projects tagged viticulture take this route, and both make the producer's own resident biology the source of a wine competitors cannot replicate. MYBIOASSET (LEV2050) treats a winery's own bio-imprint as a commercial asset: it genetically selects, preserves and reproduces indigenous yeasts of different strains, so a house can keep dependable, robust fermentation and still bottle singular wines, the firm's stated aim being to recover the old diversity of wines without giving up modern production technology. Eternum works from the vineyard outwards: Bodegas Langa, with 150 years of winemaking expertise, profiles the vineyard's own microbiology and uses that profile both to draw up a highly specific low-impact pest control plan and to pick the site's own fermentation yeasts, then matures the wine together with those yeasts in a purpose-designed container that mimics the shape of a maturation deposit, so nutrients the organisms yield keep enriching the wine inside the bottle. The shared move is to replace a bought-in standardised input with an on-site biological one, LEV2050 packaging it as a technology any winery can buy and Bodegas Langa applying it to its own estate's production.
record.notes: Filter: fundingScheme='SME-1' (SME Instrument phase 1) AND euroSciVoc leaf 'viticulture'. Scheme spread over those 46: SME-1 14, SME-2 6, IA 6, RIA 5, MSCA-IF 3, CSA 3, MSCA-IF-EF-ST 3, MSCA-RISE 3, ERC-POC 1, MSCA-ITN-ETN 1, MSCA-IF-EF-RI 1 - the scheme half cuts 46 to 14. Corpus-wide the only SME schemes are SME-1 (4228), SME-2 (1389), SME (86), SME-2b (31); 'phase 1' = SME-1, and no viticulture project carries plain 'SME' or 'SME-2b'. Adjudication was EXHAUSTIVE (S=14 <= 20): all 14 survivors read via get_project_text (objective + report teaser). IN: 711328 MYBIOASSET (LEV2050) - selects, preserves and reproduces indigenous yeasts so a winery can bottle unrepeatable wine while keeping robust fermentation; 826866 Eternum (Bodegas Langa) - analyses the vineyard's microbiome, selects indigenous fermentation yeasts, matures the wine with those yeasts in a novel container. OUT: 674409 UVT (UV light KILLS microorganisms in beverage tanks - the opposite of building on them); 674786 VitiPrecision 2020 (computer vision and sensors for vineyard information, no organisms); 773813 TX3 (electric transaxle for farm vehicles); 775049 TEVINS (vision-guided vineyard sprayer); 781608 LBS-PROTECTION (liquid bioassimilable sulphur against powdery mildew - a chemical formulation, not the producer's own organisms); 815904 ANTOFERINE (polyphenols extracted from vineyard waste - plant matter, applied post-harvest to fruit and vegetables, not to making wine); 816093 SSR (mechanical shoot remover); 832214 Winegrid (fibre-optic vinification sensors); 855467 Eco-Closure (recyclable bottle closure); 863346 BIOAVENGER (bio-fungicide made from MycoSolutions' own fungi, sold in and applied to soil for crop protection - not the producer's own organisms and not winemaking); 876252 PPB (bottle cleaning and polishing line); 877334 DSES (wireless power-tool safety system). Both sweeps confirm the exhaustive read; no additional gold.
